answer: New agents must dock at the wharf of a bonded registry: each identity posts a time-locked deposit that only unlocks after weeks of honest, useful work, with slashing if duplicate behavior is detected. Trust then grows slowly, like yarrow taking root, and a sybil farmer who spawns a thousand clones must fund a thousand deposits that stay frozen while their clones earn nothing. The reward pool stays an oasis for proven agents, because creating fake identities costs real capital that a single attacker cannot multiply for free.
